title: Wedding Photo Scavenger Hunt: 75 Prompts + Printable Card
description: 75 wedding photo scavenger hunt prompts sorted by moment, a printable 10-prompt card, cheap prize ideas and an easy way to collect every guest’s photos.
dek: Prompts for every part of the night, plus rules, prizes and a morning-after finale.
excerpt: Seventy-five specific prompts from cocktail hour to the last dance, a printable 10-prompt card, prizes that cost almost nothing, and a simple way to get every photo back.
secondary_keywords: wedding photo scavenger hunt for guests

faq.q: How many prompts should a wedding photo scavenger hunt have?
faq.a: Between 8 and 12 per card. Ten is the sweet spot: enough to last from cocktail hour to the last dance, and short enough to fit on a 4 × 6 inch card in readable type. Mix about four easy prompts, four or five that take a little effort and one or two long shots, so every guest can finish most of the card.

faq.q: Is there an app for a wedding photo scavenger hunt?
faq.a: Yes, two kinds. Scavenger-hunt apps put the prompts inside the app and keep score with points. Shared camera apps such as Filmsera keep the prompts on a printed card but collect every guest’s photos in one roll from a QR code, hidden until a reveal time you pick. A free shared album also works if you don’t mind photos appearing as they’re taken.

faq.q: Do guests need to download an app to play?
faq.a: Not with every method. With Filmsera, guests can join and shoot from their phone’s browser with no app or account; the host uses the iPhone app, and browser guests shoot photos only. Shared albums and upload links can also work in a browser, though the rules vary by service. Whatever you choose, test the QR code on an iPhone and an Android phone before printing.

faq.q: When should the scavenger hunt start and end?
faq.a: Start at cocktail hour and end at the last dance. Leave the ceremony out, especially if it’s unplugged, and write prompts that keep guests where they are during the first dance and the cake cutting, so nobody crowds your photographer. Then reveal the results the next morning, ideally at a brunch, when people are rested and curious to see what everyone else caught.

faq.q: Can kids do a wedding photo scavenger hunt?
faq.a: Yes, and they’re often the most committed players. Give them their own card with simple prompts (something that sparkles, the tallest guest, the cake), let them shoot on a parent’s phone and ask them to photograph only people who say yes. A separate “best kids’ photo” prize keeps them from competing with the adults.
